Reads text directly via the accessibility service: exact, instant, and offline. Works only in apps that report character coordinates; other apps and images fall back to screen recognition.\n\nExperimental: inaccurate coordinates from some apps can misalign highlights or select adjacent words. Screen recognition is disabled; reads only text exposed to accessibility services. Images, manga, games, and unsupported apps are ignored.\n\nIntended for e-ink devices, low-end hardware, and metered connections: zero recognition overhead or network usage.

Sends cropped screen regions to cloud recognition at higher relative resolution to detect small text missed by full-screen scans. Increases network requests and data usage.

On demand: scans the region under the aim point when held over an area where the initial scan found no text.

Always: splits the entire screen into regions on every scan (uses more data).
Instant on-device draft refined by cloud recognition. Falls back to on-device when offline.
Highest accuracy; minimal storage and battery use. Requires internet.
Fully offline; zero network traffic. Slightly lower accuracy on complex fonts.
Forced Offline Mode is active. Locked to on-device recognition.

Both: runs on-device and cloud recognition in parallel. On-device recognition yields an immediate draft around the aim point, then cloud recognition replaces it. Retains the on-device result when offline or on error.

Cloud: requires a network connection; results appear after the server responds.

Device: offline only; lower accuracy on vertical text and manga; OCR boost is unavailable.
Starts full-screen on-device recognition only if cloud recognition has not responded within 3 s. Reduces CPU and battery usage; words away from the aim point appear later.

Apps cannot restart accessibility services automatically. Open accessibility settings and toggle Screenlate off and on.

Aggressive background restrictions can terminate the accessibility service. An ongoing notification makes termination less likely.
Does not guarantee immunity from termination. If stopped, toggle the service off and on in accessibility settings.

Resets all settings to defaults: bubble, hidden apps, lookup, Anki, audio, field templates, popup (font selection, sizes, CSS), translation, Chinese script, theme, colors, e-ink mode, background work, and update notices. Dismissed hints reappear. Dictionaries, enabled languages, installed fonts, and app language are kept.
Bubble settings, hidden apps, size, and screen position will be reset to defaults. If hidden, the bubble will become visible.
Scan length, result limit, and all other lookup settings will be reset to defaults.
Deck, note type, field templates, tags, and duplicate rules will be reset to defaults. AnkiDroid data is unaffected.
Header display, definition copying, auto-hide, font selection, text size and weight, and custom CSS will be reset to defaults. Installed fonts are kept.
Translation button, note translation, service order and states, target language, and favorites will be reset to defaults.
Theme reverts to system, colors reset to defaults, and e-ink mode is disabled (restoring previous sizes). App language is kept.
Persistent notification will be disabled. System battery and autostart settings are unaffected.
%1$s: import stopped after the app closed twice. Try again; repeated failure may indicate a corrupted or oversized file.
Bundled dictionary installation stopped after the app closed twice. Scheduled to retry after the next update, or tap “Retry” to try now.
Dictionary reset stopped after the app closed twice. Some dictionaries may remain or be missing; manage them manually in Dictionaries.
Screenlate uses the accessibility service to display the floating bubble over other apps and read on-screen text.

• Screenshots on bubble tap or drag (with App text only: solely for Anki note images).\n• On-screen app text on the same triggers when Read app text or App text only is enabled.\n• Active app package, keyboard, and system bar bounds to respect hidden apps and avoid UI overlap.

• Screenshots are sent to cloud recognition unless Engines is set to Device or App text only is enabled. On-device recognition transmits nothing.
• Sentences are sent to an online translator when triggered via the translation button or a note template.
• Terms and readings are sent to configured audio sources for pronunciation.
• Notes are exported locally to AnkiDroid.

The service performs no automated taps or input. Captured data is not stored: screenshots remain in memory only until the bubble docks, Anki notes receive only the selected crop, and logs exclude screen text.
On-device recognition uses per-language models. ML Kit is bundled; other models require download and selection in the language list. Cloud recognition does not use local models.
No on-device model supports this language.
Downloaded models activate upon selection. Switch to another model before deleting an active one.
Bundled; no download required. Supports Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Devanagari, Bengali, and Latin scripts.
Lower accuracy on complex backgrounds; cloud recognition is recommended.

The main model handles on-device recognition. Other checked models are downloaded for later selection in Text recognition settings. Bundled ML Kit supports Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Devanagari, Bengali, and Latin scripts as the default when no other main model is selected.
